source_statement: This contract was derived from vendor REFERENCE DOCUMENTATION, not from a published API specification. VCF Automation - the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation - has no OpenAPI document in the Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository and offers no downloadable specification for the Catalog service on the Broadcom Developer Portal. Every statement below was transcribed by hand from the rendered xAPIs pages recorded in docs/official_sources.json, each with the URL, the operation it documents and the date it was fetched. Where the documentation is silent this contract makes an explicit local decision and labels it as such under 'local_decisions'. Treat this file, not the live portal, as authoritative for this exercise.
base_url: Runtime-supplied. The reference pages render the host as https://{api_host}; no host is baked into this contract.

operations.id_provenance: Contract-local identifier. The reference pages render a human title, not a machine operationId, because no specification is published. The rendered title is 'Get Catalog Items' and the rendered summary is 'Fetch a list of catalog items'.
operations.title: Get Catalog Items
operations.summary: Fetch a list of catalog items

forbidden.name: Content-Type
forbidden.reason: The operation has no request body.

forbidden.name: Content-Length
forbidden.reason: The operation has no request body. A zero-valued header is still a violation.

query_parameters.name: page
query_parameters.contract_usage: always sent, explicitly, starting at 0 and advancing by exactly 1

query_parameters.name: size
query_parameters.documented_description: The size of the page to be returned
query_parameters.contract_usage: always sent, explicitly, identical on every request of one collection walk

query_parameters.name: sort
query_parameters.documented_description: Sorting criteria in the format: property,(asc|desc)
query_parameters.contract_usage: always sent exactly once with the literal value name,asc

query_parameters.name: search
query_parameters.documented_description: Matches will have this string somewhere in their name or description
query_parameters.contract_usage: sent once, unchanged on every page, only when the caller supplies a search term; otherwise absent

query_parameters.name: projects
query_parameters.documented_description: A list of project IDs to filter by
query_parameters.contract_usage: when the caller supplies project ids, sent as one repeated parameter per id in caller order, unchanged on every page; otherwise absent

query_parameters.name: types
query_parameters.documented_description: A list of Catalog Item Type IDs to filter by

query_parameters.name: expand
query_parameters.documented_description: The expanded details of the requested comma separated objects

query_parameters.name: $top
query_parameters.contract_usage: never sent by this client; page/size pagination is used instead

query_parameters.name: $skip
query_parameters.documented_description: Number of records you want to skip
query_parameters.contract_usage: never sent by this client; page/size pagination is used instead

query_parameters.name: $orderby
query_parameters.documented_description: Sorting criteria in the format: property (asc|desc)
query_parameters.contract_usage: never sent by this client; sort is used instead

operations.omission_rule: Any query parameter whose contract_usage is 'never sent' or whose caller-supplied value is absent MUST be omitted from the query string entirely. Omitted means the parameter name does not appear at all. Sending the name with an empty value, a zero, a false, the string 'null', or a bare delimiter is a contract violation, not an omission.

query_serialisation.order_note: Parameters are emitted in exactly this relative order. Repeated projects parameters keep caller order among themselves.
query_serialisation.percent_encoding: UTF-8 percent-encoding. The comma in the sort value is percent-encoded, so sort is transmitted as sort=name%2Casc. Reserved characters in caller-supplied values, notably &, are percent-encoded so that they cannot be read as parameter delimiters.

members.number: int32, the zero-based index of the page actually returned
members.numberOfElements: int32, the number of elements on this page
members.size: int32, the page size actually applied
members.totalElements: int64, the number of elements across every page

ResourceReference.note: Every member is optional, so a CatalogItem.type object carrying no id is well formed and must not be treated as an error.

excluded_routes.title: Get Catalog Items For Admin
excluded_routes.reason: A distinct administrative route with a different parameter set (sourceIds, projectId). Outside this contract.

excluded_routes.title: Find a catalog item with specified ID
excluded_routes.reason: Per-item lookup. The collection must be assembled from the paginated route alone.

local_decisions: The reference pages document page, size and sort as optional with defaults. This contract requires page and size to be sent explicitly on every request so that the walk is self-describing and reproducible rather than dependent on server defaults.
The reference pages document sort only by format, 'property,(asc|desc)'. This contract fixes the single value name,asc.

The reference pages do not state a percent-encoding convention. This contract fixes UTF-8 percent-encoding and requires the comma in the sort value to be encoded as %2C so that the raw query string is unambiguous.
The reference pages do not state a query parameter order. This contract fixes the order page, size, sort, search, projects.
The reference pages document a minimum page size of 1 but no maximum. This contract accepts any integer page size of 1 or greater and rejects anything below 1 before any request is sent.

The reference pages do not describe client-side ordering. This contract requires the assembled collection to be ordered by name then id, ascending and case-sensitive, because sort=name,asc leaves the relative order of equal names unspecified and therefore unstable across a paginated walk.
